Subject: Vendr profile: metadata retention & field mapping clarification

Hi Sophie,

Thanks for onboarding Bluecrest into Vendr last week — appreciate the quick turnaround. We're doing a final pass before we attach Vendr profile links to the customer's SOC 2 evidence bundle and have a couple of clarifying asks around metadata and retention settings so our security intake team can map fields to the CAIQ/SIG controls. Can you confirm the following?

1) Field canonicalization: which profile fields are considered the canonical source for (a) service endpoints, (b) data residency, and (c) temporary credential TTLs? We want to avoid ambiguous mappings when we extract for audits.

2) Retention windows: does Vendr maintain historical snapshots of profile metadata (change history) and for how long? We're particularly trying to understand if we can reconstruct the profile state from 90/180/365 days ago for audit timelines.

3) Proof-of-possession for ephemeral creds: Bluecrest uses short-lived service accounts that are uploaded as artifacts in the profile. For our SOC 2 evidence we need a signed statement from Vendr confirming whether you store PW/keys or only proof-of-possession hashes and the retention/custody policy.

4) Export formats: can you provide a machine-friendly export (CSV/JSON/XLSX) of the profile field map with canonical names and mapping to CAIQ/SIG questions? If you already have a mapping sheet, that would be perfect.

Attachments: I tried to capture our desired schema in a sample mapping (not exhaustive) — attached as a starter: vendr_metadata_field_map.xlsx (sample column names we expect).

Would you be able to respond by EOD Wednesday so we can progress the evidence bundle? If helpful, we can hop on a short 20-minute call with Rishi (security) and Mina (portal ops) to go through the specifics.

Thanks —
Chloe

Hi Chloe — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below; forwarding to our security team for the signed statement you requested.

On 19 May 2028, at 09:12, Chloe Martin wrote:
> 1) Field canonicalization: which profile fields are considered the canonical source for (a) service endpoints, (b) data residency, and (c) temporary credential TTLs?

- Service endpoints: canonical field is `service_endpoint` (profile export column: service_endpoint).
- Data residency: canonical field is `data_region` (export column: data_region, values: us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1).
- Temporary credential TTLs: canonical field is `ephemeral_ttl_seconds` (we store as integer seconds; default is 3600 unless customer overrides).

> 2) Retention windows: does Vendr maintain historical snapshots of profile metadata (change history) and for how long?

- Yes, we retain a change history for profile metadata. Default retention is 365 days for metadata diffs; full snapshot exports are kept for 90 days. If a customer purchases extended retention (add-on), we can extend to 3 years — Bluecrest does not have that add-on enabled.

> 3) Proof-of-possession for ephemeral creds: ... need a signed statement ... confirming whether you store PW/keys or only proof-of-possession hashes and the retention/custody policy.

- We DO NOT store plaintext secrets. For uploads marked as "ephemeral_key" we persist a SHA-256 hash and associated proof-of-possession metadata (uploader, upload timestamp). The actual secret is only stored in transit to the customer's configured S3 and is not kept on Vendr. I'll have our security team attach a signed PDF that explains custody and retention.

> 4) Export formats: can you provide a machine-friendly export (CSV/JSON/XLSX) of the profile field map with canonical names and mapping to CAIQ/SIG questions?

- Attached is a canonical field map (vendr_metadata_field_map.xlsx) and a short retention policy PDF. The field map includes a column 'caiaq_mapping' with links to the CAIQ question ids.

I'll follow up with the signed statement within 24–48 hours. If you'd like to review the sheet together, I'm available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Best,
Sophie

Thanks Sophie — that helps. Two follow-ups from the security review team: 

• Can you confirm the retention policy for the SHA-256 hashes for ephemeral keys? We need to know whether hashes are purged when the associated credential is rotated/deleted by the customer, or retained for the full 365-day metadata window.

• For the change-history snapshots (365 days), do those snapshots include the `ephemeral_ttl_seconds` value at time-of-change, or is that field redacted in snapshots? For audit reconstruction we need the TTL recorded.

Also: when you attach the signed custody statement, please include a brief paragraph that explicitly states "Vendr does not retain plaintext secrets uploaded as ephemeral credentials; only cryptographic proofs (SHA-256) and metadata are stored" and the contact name/email for escalation.

If it's easier to add those lines to the PDF and re-send, that'll close this loop. We can then ingest the mapping sheet into our SIG->evidence crosswalk.

—Rishi

Rishi / Chloe — attaching the signed possession statement and a short addendum that answers your two follow-ups. Excerpt included below for quick reference.

--- Forwarded attachment: signed-possession-statement.pdf ---
Vendr confirms: we do not store plaintext secrets. SHA-256 hashes associated with ephemeral_key uploads are retained for the configured metadata retention window (standard: 365 days) and will be purged after that period or sooner if the customer requests an immediate purge via the profile deletion API. The `ephemeral_ttl_seconds` value is included in change-history snapshots and preserved in the 365-day metadata window. For escalation: Security contact — security@vendr.com (ops lead: Todd Pierce).

If those terms are acceptable I'll mark the Vendr profile as ready for ingestion into the Bluecrest evidence bundle and send the profile export CSV.

Sophie
